simple.meaning: רֵחֶה (rêcheh) is a Hebrew object word meaning “a mill -stone.” BibleIQ follows the concrete thing through the verses where it appears.
simple.biblicalBackground: The occurrence trail begins at Exodus 11:5. The surrounding context includes birth, firstborn, land, Egypt.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to רֵחֶה (H7347) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Concrete words often carry patterns through Scripture because objects, animals, offerings, and created things are used repeatedly in worship, judgment, covenant, and narrative.
simple.summary: רֵחֶה (rêcheh) / H7347 is traced through Exodus 11:5, Numbers 11:8, Deuteronomy 24:6, Isaiah 47:2 with generated occurrence evidence.

definitions.full: H7347. recheh [ רֵחַה ] noun [masculine] , only dual רֵחַיִם (hand-)mill (probably = two mill-stones ); — ׳ר absolute, common household utensil, turned by maids, Exod 11:5 ( הָרֵחָ֑יִלם ; J), female slaves Isa 47:1 (with טָחַן , q. v.); בָּר ׳טָחַן Num 11:8 (J); ׳ר וָרָ֑כֶב Deut 24:6 (see רכב ); ר ׳קוֺל as sound of family life Jer 25:10 .
definitions.rootNote: from an unused root meaning to pulverize ;

occurrences.englishText: and all the firstborn in the land of Egypt shall die, from the firstborn of Pharaoh who sits on his throne, even to the firstborn of the female servant who is behind the mill, and all the firstborn of livestock.
The people went around, gathered it, and ground it in mills, or beat it in mortars, and boiled it in pots, and made cakes of it. Its taste was like the taste of fresh oil.
No man shall take the mill or the upper millstone as a pledge, for he takes a life in pledge.
Take the millstones and grind flour.
Moreover I will take from them the voice of mirth and the voice of gladness, the voice of the bridegroom and the voice of the bride, the sound of the millstones, and the light of the lamp.
